costfun.Description: Define the type of cost function.

sensor_power_load_no_var_loads.friendly_name: Sensor power loads with no variable loads
sensor_power_load_no_var_loads.Description: The name of the household power consumption sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. The deferrable loads that we will want to include in the optimization problem should be subtracted from this sensor in HASS. For example: ‘sensor.power_load_no_var_loads’

sensor_power_load_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases (System) is 2 or 3. One uncontrolled household load power entity_id per phase (Watts), index-matched L1, L2, L3 - for example from a DSMR/P1 smart meter's per-phase power sensors. Unlike PV, there is no safe default split for the uncontrolled load if this is left blank: a warning is logged and that phase's base load is treated as 0 in the per-phase safety cap - fuse-overload protection then only covers phase-tagged deferrable loads/batteries, not your other (uncontrolled) household consumption on that phase.

sensor_replace_zero.friendly_name: Sensor to replace NAN values with 0s
sensor_replace_zero.Description: The list of retrieved variables that we would want to replace NANs (if they exist) with zeros.

sensor_linear_interp.friendly_name: Sensor to replace NAN values with linear interpolation
sensor_linear_interp.Description: The list of retrieved variables that we would want to interpolate NANs values using linear interpolation

ssl_no_verify.Description: Set to true to disable SSL verification when connecting to Home Assistant. Useful if using self-signed certificates (HTTPS with IP address).

use_websocket.friendly_name: Use Home Assistant websocket for data retrieval
use_websocket.Description: Enable Home Assistant websocket as data source instead of Home Assistant API. This allows for longer historical data retention and better performance for machine learning models.

use_influxdb.Description: Enable InfluxDB as data source instead of Home Assistant API. This allows for longer historical data retention and better performance for machine learning models. Only supports version 1.x.

influxdb_host.Description: The IP address or hostname of your InfluxDB instance. Defaults to localhost.

influxdb_port.Description: The port number for your InfluxDB instance. Defaults to 8086.

influxdb_database.Description: The name of the InfluxDB database containing your Home Assistant data. Defaults to 'homeassistant'.

influxdb_measurement.Description: The measurement name where your sensor data is stored. Defaults to 'W' for the Home Assistant integration.

influxdb_retention_policy.Description: The retention policy to use for InfluxDB queries. Defaults to 'autogen'.

influxdb_use_ssl.Description: Enables HTTPS on InfluxDB connections. Defaults to 'false'.

influxdb_verify_ssl.Description: Enables SSL verification of the certificate (e.g. Let's Encrypt) on InfluxDB connections. Defaults to 'false'.

continual_publish.Description: set to True to save entities to .json after an optimization run. Then automatically republish the saved entities (with updated current state value) every freq minutes. entity data saved to data_path/entities.

logging_level.Description: DEBUG provides detailed diagnostic information, INFO gives general operational messages, WARNING highlights potential issues, and ERROR indicates critical problems that may disrupt functionality.

optimization_time_step.Description: The time step to resample retrieved data from hass. This parameter is given in minutes. It should not be defined too low or you will run into memory problems when defining the Linear Programming optimization. Defaults to 30

historic_days_to_retrieve.Description: We will retrieve data from now to days_to_retrieve days. Defaults to 2

load_negative.Description: Set this parameter to True if the retrieved load variable is negative by convention. Defaults to False

set_zero_min.Description: Set this parameter to True to give a special treatment for a minimum value saturation to zero for power consumption data. Values below zero are replaced by nans. Defaults to True.

method_ts_round.Description: Set the method for timestamp rounding, options are: first, last and nearest.

delta_forecast_daily.Description: The number of days for forecasted data; can be overridden at runtime via runtimeparams. Defaults to 1. For naive-mpc, the forecast window is now extended automatically to cover a longer prediction_horizon, so this parameter usually need not be set manually for multi-day MPC runs.

load_forecast_method.Description: The load forecast method that will be used. The options are ‘csv’ to load a CSV file or ‘naive’ for a simple 1-day persistence model.

load_forecast_quantile_bias.Description: Blend factor that biases the load forecast toward a conservative P90 (high) estimate. 0 (default) uses the central P50 estimate, i.e. unchanged behaviour. 1 uses the P90 estimate. Intermediate values blend linearly: estimate = bias*P90 + (1-bias)*P50. Unlike the PV bias (where conservative means less generation, P10), a conservative load estimate means more consumption, P90 - the tail that actually threatens grid-import/battery-sizing constraints. The P90 is built via top-down temporal reconciliation: a historically-informed daily total is disaggregated back down to each timestep using the shape of the point forecast, so the reconciled timesteps sum to that daily total instead of each independently assuming its own worst case at once. Works with any load_forecast_method. Defaults to 0.

load_quantile_spread_refit_window_days.friendly_name: Load forecast P10/P90 spread refit window
load_quantile_spread_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of your own sensor_power_load_no_var_loads history the load-quantile-spread-refit action uses to learn the P10/P90 spread ratios. Learned separately for each period of the day (night/morning/afternoon/evening - night load barely varies day to day, evening load varies a lot). Day-of-week (weekend-or-weekday, then the exact day) and time-of-year (season, then the exact month) are learned as two independent multiplicative corrections rather than one combined bucket, since they're separate sources of variability - each axis's own levels are blended by how many days of evidence they have (a handful of unusual days can't dominate outright), then the two axes are combined together, and blended in turn with a generic bundled reference dataset used until you've built up your own history. Defaults to 180.

load_quantile_spread_refit_forgetting_fa.friendly_name: Load forecast P10/P90 spread refit forgetting factor
load_quantile_spread_refit_forgetting_fa.Description: Weight (0-1) given to the previously-learned load quantile-spread ratios each time load-quantile-spread-refit runs, blended against this window's own estimate - a household's routine genuinely drifts over time (a new appliance, a schedule change), so old evidence fades out gradually across refits instead of a bucket's value jumping straight to whatever the latest window computes, or disappearing the moment its data ages out of the window. Higher = slower, more stable convergence across refits; lower = faster response to new data but noisier. Defaults to 0.7.

mlforecaster_weather_features.Description: Optional list of weather covariate columns to feed the 'mlforecaster' load forecast model as exogenous inputs, in addition to the always-present calendar features. Useful when the load is weather-dependent (e.g. a heat pump). Leave empty to disable (default). Supported values: temp_air, relative_humidity, cloud_cover, wind_speed, ghi, direct_radiation, diffuse_radiation, precipitation, heating_degree, cooling_degree. The values are sourced from the Open-Meteo weather forecast; heating_degree/cooling_degree are derived from the temperature. Only used when 'Load forecast method' above is mlforecaster.

num_threads.friendly_name: Number of threads to use for the LP solver
num_threads.Description: Set the number of threads for the LP solver to use, when supported by the solver. Defaults to 0 (autodetect)

lp_solver_timeout.Description: Set the maximum time (in seconds) for the LP solver. Defaults to 45.

lp_solver_mip_rel_gap.Description: For mixed-integer problems (with binary variables), the solver stops when the solution is within this percentage of optimal. Valid range: 0 to 1 (0% to 100%). Higher values (e.g., 0.05 = 5%) solve faster with minimal quality loss. Defaults to 0.01 (within 1% of optimal), which keeps deep-horizon problems from timing out without a published plan. Set to 0 for exact optimal.

open_meteo_cache_max_age.Description: The maximum age, in minutes, of the cached open-meteo json response, after which a new version will be fetched from Open-Meteo. Defaults to 30.

maximum_power_from_grid.Description: The maximum power that can be supplied by the utility grid in Watts (consumption). Defaults to 9000.

maximum_power_to_grid.Description: The maximum power that can be supplied to the utility grid in Watts (injection). Defaults to 9000.

number_of_phases.Description: How many phases your household grid connection has: 1 (single-phase) or 2/3 (multi-phase, e.g. a Dutch driefasenaansluiting). Defaults to 1. When set to 2 or 3, EMHASS additionally caps the combined power of every phase-tagged deferrable load, battery and (if configured) uncontrolled household load/PV against maximum_power_from_grid_per_phase/maximum_power_to_grid_per_phase, so a single phase's fuse is never overloaded - on top of, not instead of, the existing whole-house maximum_power_from_grid/maximum_power_to_grid limit. At 1 (the default) this entire feature is inactive and nothing behaves differently.

maximum_power_from_grid_per_phase.friendly_name: Max power from grid, per phase
maximum_power_from_grid_per_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases is 2 or 3. The maximum power any single phase (L1/L2/L3) may draw from the grid, in Watts - typically your connection's per-phase fuse rating (e.g. a 3x25A connection is about 5750W per phase). Accepts a single value, broadcast to every phase (the common case for a symmetric connection), or a list of exactly number_of_phases values for an asymmetric setup. This is additional to, not a replacement for, the whole-house maximum_power_from_grid limit above. Defaults to 4000.

maximum_power_to_grid_per_phase.friendly_name: Max export power to grid, per phase
maximum_power_to_grid_per_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases is 2 or 3. The maximum power any single phase (L1/L2/L3) may inject into the grid, in Watts. Same broadcast-or-per-phase-list shape as maximum_power_from_grid_per_phase. Additional to, not a replacement for, the whole-house maximum_power_to_grid limit above. Defaults to 4000.

load_cost_forecast_method.Description: Define the method that will be used for load cost forecast. The options are ‘hp_hc_periods’ for peak and non-peak hours contracts, and ‘csv’ to load custom cost from CSV file.

load_peak_hour_periods.Description: A list of peak hour periods for load consumption from the grid. This is useful if you have a contract with peak and non-peak hours.

load_peak_hours_cost.Description: The cost of the electrical energy during peak hours

load_offpeak_hours_cost.Description: The cost of the electrical energy during off-peak hours

capacity_cost_per_kw.Description: A cost (currency per kW) applied to the peak grid import power over the optimisation horizon, for tariffs with a capacity or demand charge. 0 (default) disables it and leaves the plan unchanged. A positive value makes the optimiser flatten the import peak, trading it off against energy cost in a single pass. The peak is priced once (it is a power charge, not energy), so set it to the marginal value of shaving 1 kW of peak.

production_price_forecast_method.friendly_name: PV power production price forecast method
production_price_forecast_method.Description: Define the method that will be used for PV power production price forecast. This is the price that is paid by the utility for energy injected into the grid. The options are ‘constant’ for a constant fixed value or ‘csv’ to load custom price forecasts from a CSV file.

photovoltaic_production_sell_price.Description: The paid price for energy injected to the grid from excess PV production in currency/kWh.

thermal_gas_price_forecast_method.Description: When the heat pump is hybrid, define the gas price as a constant fixed value or read it from a column in the thermal data CSV.

thermal_gas_price.Description: Fixed gas price in €/kWh used for hybrid heat-pump gas cost calculations.

thermal_gas_price_col.Description: Column name in the thermal data CSV containing the gas price series in €/kWh when gas price method is set to csv.

set_use_pv.Description: Set to True if we should consider an solar PV system. Defaults to False

sensor_power_photovoltaics.Description: This is the name of the photovoltaic power-produced sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. For example: ‘sensor.power_photovoltaics’.

sensor_power_photovoltaics_forecast.Description: This is the name of the photovoltaic forecast sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. For example: ‘sensor.p_pv_forecast’.

sensor_power_photovoltaics_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases (System) is 2 or 3. One PV power entity_id per phase (Watts), index-matched L1, L2, L3 - for example from a three-phase PV inverter that reports per-leg output. Optional: leave blank to have EMHASS assume PV production is split evenly across all phases (a reasonable default for a symmetric three-phase inverter).

sensor_power_photovoltaics_per_panel.Description: Optional: one PV power entity_id per physical panel (Watts) - for example from optimizers or microinverters. When set, the pv-horizon-refit action also learns a shading profile per panel, in addition to the combined system profile - useful to localize a fixed, partial obstruction (a chimney affecting only some panels) that the combined sensor_power_photovoltaics alone cannot distinguish from a full-width one. Diagnostics only: shown in the pv-horizon-refit result, not applied to the forecast. Two supported setups, chosen by how many entries the plant config holds - not by which brand of hardware, but by whether the panels each have their own independent AC-side inverter: a single PV orientation group (surface_azimuth/surface_tilt/etc each holding one value) - each panel's expected output approximates the combined simulation divided by the module count; correct for a DC optimizer system (SolarEdge, Tigo and similar), since those still share one central string inverter for the actual DC-to-AC conversion and clipping, even though each panel is individually monitored. Or one orientation-group entry per panel (surface_azimuth/surface_tilt/pv_module_model/pv_inverter_model/modules_per_string/strings_per_inverter each holding exactly as many entries as this list, in the same order as the physical panels here) - each panel then gets its own exact PVLib simulation, correctly capped at its own rating; only physically correct for true microinverters (e.g. Enphase), where each panel has its own independent AC-side conversion and clipping ceiling.

set_use_adjusted_pv.Description: Set to True if we should consider an adjusted solar PV system. Defaults to False

adjusted_pv_regression_model.Description: Set the type of regression model that will be used to adjust the solar PV production to local conditions. Available models are defined in REGRESSION_METHODS (machine_learning_regressor.py). Defaults to LassoRegression

adjusted_pv_solar_elevation_threshold.Description: This is the solar elevation threshold parameter used to identify the early morning or late evening periods. Defaults to 10.

adjusted_pv_model_max_age.Description: Maximum age in hours before the adjusted PV regression model is re-fitted. If the saved model is older than this value, a new model will be trained using fresh historical data. Set to 0 to force re-fitting on every call. Defaults to 24 hours (1 day).

pv_module_model.Description: The PV module model. Enter the exact CEC database name, or enter the nominal power in Watts (e.g., 300) to automatically use the closest matching panel. Can be a list for mixed orientation systems.

pv_inverter_model.Description: The PV inverter model. Enter the exact CEC database name, or enter the nominal AC power in Watts (e.g., 5000) to automatically use the closest matching inverter. Can be a list for mixed orientation systems.

surface_tilt.Description: The tilt angle of your solar panels. Defaults to 30. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

surface_azimuth.Description: The azimuth of your PV installation. Defaults to 205. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

modules_per_string.Description: The number of modules per string. Defaults to 16. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

strings_per_inverter.Description: The number of used strings per inverter. Defaults to 1. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

pv_inverter_group.Description: Per-entry group id (0 = none) for PV plant config entries (pv_module_model/surface_tilt/surface_azimuth/etc) that share one physical inverter - e.g. a central inverter with multiple independently-tracked MPPT strings, or DC-optimizer strings landing on separate MPPT inputs of the same inverter. Entries with the same non-zero group id are simulated together with one shared inverter (correctly applying its AC clipping ceiling once to their combined output) instead of each getting its own independent copy of the inverter. Leave at the default (0, or omit) for the common case where every entry already represents its own independent inverter (including true microinverter systems).

weather_forecast_method.Description: This will define the weather forecast method that will be used. options are 'open-meteo', 'Solcast', 'solar.forecast' (forecast.solar) and 'csv' to load a CSV file. When loading a CSV file this will be directly considered as the PV power forecast in Watts.

weather_forecast_pv_quantile_bias.Description: Blend factor that biases the PV forecast toward a conservative P10 (low) estimate. 0 (default) uses the central P50 estimate, i.e. unchanged behaviour. 1 uses the P10 estimate. Intermediate values blend linearly: estimate = bias*P10 + (1-bias)*P50. Higher values produce more defensive plans (more battery reserve held when solar is uncertain). Effective with weather_forecast_method set to solcast (Solcast's own P10), or set to open-meteo with open_meteo_pv_ensemble_enabled also on (an Open-Meteo ensemble-derived P10 - see that setting). A no-op, with a warning, for any other method/combination. Defaults to 0.

open_meteo_pv_ensemble_enabled.Description: Off (default): no effect. On: when weather_forecast_method is open-meteo, also fetches Open-Meteo's Ensemble API (multiple perturbed weather scenarios from ECMWF/GFS/ICON) to derive a P10 (conservative, low) PV estimate for the weather_forecast_pv_quantile_bias blend - the same conservative-bias mechanism Solcast's own P10 already feeds. Requires weather_forecast_pv_quantile_bias > 0 to actually change anything. Each candidate model's forecast accuracy is tracked over time (forward-accumulating - Open-Meteo doesn't retain historical ensemble data to backtest against) and used to weight its contribution; a model starts at equal weight until enough of its own forecasts have resolved against real production. Costs 3 extra API calls and 1 extra PV simulation per forecast cycle.

pv_horizon_learning_enabled.Description: Off (default): the PV forecast assumes a fully open sky, as always. On: the pv-horizon-refit action's learned per-direction horizon profile (trees, chimneys, neighbouring roofs) is applied to mask direct sunlight below the learned elevation at each compass direction. Has no effect until pv-horizon-refit has actually been run at least once - a missing profile silently means no masking, same as off.

pv_horizon_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of actual PV production + Open-Meteo historical weather the pv-horizon-refit action compares against an unobstructed clear-sky simulation to learn the shading/horizon profile. Defaults to 60.

pv_horizon_refit_forgetting_factor.Description: Weight (0-1) given to the previously-learned horizon profile each time pv-horizon-refit runs, blended against this window's own estimate. Higher = slower, more stable convergence across refits; lower = faster response to new data but noisier. Defaults to 0.7.

set_total_pv_sell.Description: Set this parameter to true to consider that all the PV power produced is injected to the grid. No direct self-consumption. The default is false, for a system with direct self-consumption.

compute_curtailment.Description: Set to True to compute a special PV curtailment variable (Default False). When enabled, curtailment that is cost-equivalent is scheduled as late as possible in the optimization horizon

ignore_pv_feedback_during_curtailment.Description: When set to true, prevents PV forecast from being updated with real PV data, avoiding flip-flop behavior during curtailment operations

inverter_is_hybrid.Description: Set to True to consider that the installation inverter is hybrid for PV and batteries (Default False)

inverter_ac_output_max.friendly_name: Max hybrid inverter AC output power
inverter_ac_output_max.Description: Maximum hybrid inverter output power from combined PV and battery discharge.

inverter_ac_input_max.friendly_name: Max hybrid inverter AC input power
inverter_ac_input_max.Description: Maximum hybrid inverter input power from grid to charge battery.

inverter_efficiency_dc_ac.friendly_name: Hybrid inverter efficency DC to AC
inverter_efficiency_dc_ac.Description: Hybrid inverter efficiency from the DC bus to AC output. (percentage/100)

inverter_efficiency_ac_dc.friendly_name: Hybrid inverter efficency AC to DC
inverter_efficiency_ac_dc.Description: Hybrid inverter efficiency when charging from the AC input to DC bus. (percentage/100)

inverter_stress_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh) applied at the inverter's nominal power to penalise high loads. Currently implemented as a quadratic curve (Cost ∝ Power²), incentivising 'low and slow' operation to reduce thermal stress and smooth power flows.

inverter_stress_segments.Description: The number of linear segments used to approximate the stress cost curve. Higher values increase accuracy but may slightly increase computation time.

number_of_deferrable_loads.Description: Define the number of deferrable loads (appliances to shift) to consider. Defaults to 1 - add more with the load tabs below as needed.

load_names.Description: Name per load tab (for example: Washing Machine, Dishwasher, Pool Pump).

load_type.Description: Select the control profile per load: program-based cycle (washer/dryer/dishwasher), fixed power splittable over time (e-bike charging), fixed power non-splittable block, or variable power and variable time.

load_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases (System) is 2 or 3. Which physical phase(s) this load is wired to - a fixed property of your home's wiring, not something EMHASS chooses. A single value (L1/L2/L3) for a load on one leg, or a '+'-joined combination (e.g. 'L1+L2' for a 2-phase appliance, 'L1+L2+L3' for a fully 3-phase one) for a load wired across more than one phase - its power is then assumed evenly split across the named phases rather than counted on just one. Leave blank ('') to leave this load out of the per-phase power cap entirely (the default - fully backward compatible). Loads left unassigned are not protected against overloading a phase.

load_washdata_enabled.Description: Only relevant for the 'program_based' load type above. Enable to link this load to a real appliance tracked by the WashData 'ha_washdata' custom integration, revealing the device picker below instead of hand-typing programs/power values.

load_washdata_device.Description: Only shown when 'Use a WashData device' above is enabled. Pick the appliance tracked by the WashData 'ha_washdata' custom integration (matching its sensor.<device>_profiel_<program>_aantal / binary_sensor.<device>_actief entities). EMHASS discovers every learned program for that device fresh each optimization cycle (unlike most other per-load fields, this is never frozen at config-save time), and uses the most-used program's learned power_profile/power_profile_interval_min - and its implied duration - instead of this load's flat nominal_power_of_deferrable_loads/operating_hours_of_each_deferrable_load. See 'Program select sensor' below to pin a specific program instead of the most-used one. Falls back gracefully to the flat model if no learned program is found yet.

manual_load_enabled.Description: Master switch for the manually-committed load behaviour below. Enables appliances that have no smart-plug control (e.g. a washing machine or dishwasher with only a physical delay-start timer) to be marked manual per-load via 'Manually-committed load'. When a manual load's ready sensor is turned on, EMHASS computes an optimal start time once and publishes it as an instruction - that commitment is then pinned and will not move on later re-optimizations, since the user has already physically set the appliance's timer.

is_manual_load.Description: One per deferrable load. Enable to treat this load as manually-committed: EMHASS uses this load's own name/nominal power/operating hours (or its resolved WashData profile, if 'Use a WashData device' above is enabled) together with the ready/confirmation/program-select sensors below, instead of scheduling it automatically like a normal deferrable load. Requires 'Enable manually-committed loads' to be on.

manual_load_ready_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. The Home Assistant entity ID of an input_boolean (or similar) that the user turns on to signal they want this load to run. EMHASS reads this each optimization cycle to decide whether to commit a start time for that load.

manual_load_program_select_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load and 'WashData device' above resolved more than one learned program. The Home Assistant entity ID of a select you set to the program you're about to run (e.g. select.wasmachine_cyclusprogramma, an entity WashData already provides). EMHASS matches its current option against the discovered programs and pins the plan to that exact one; without it, or while it's left on "auto_detect", EMHASS falls back to the most-used discovered program.

manual_load_deadline_hour.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. Optional latest time of day this load must be finished by. Leave empty to allow scheduling anywhere in the optimization horizon.

manual_load_confirm_power_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. Optional Home Assistant entity ID of a power sensor (e.g. a smart plug that can measure but not safely switch the appliance). When set, EMHASS uses it only to detect that the appliance has actually started, to automatically clear the commitment - never to control the appliance.

load_dispatch_mode.Description: Per-load optimization mode: hours (runtime via operating hours) or energy_kwh (deliver target energy). Program-based sequencing is controlled by the load type itself.

load_programs.Description: For program_based loads: JSON list of programs. Each program has name and power_pattern (comma-separated watts per step).

required_energy_kwh_of_each_deferrable_l.Description: Used when dispatch mode is energy_kwh. Defines energy that must be delivered during the optimization horizon.

nominal_power_of_deferrable_loads.Description: The nominal (calculated max) power for each deferrable load in Watts.

minimum_power_of_deferrable_loads.Description: The minimum power for each deferrable load in Watts.

cost_forecast_per_deferrable_load.Description: Optional per-deferrable-load cost forecast track (Currency/kWh) that overrides the shared load_cost_forecast for that specific load - works for any deferrable load, not just heating. Useful whenever one load is priced differently than the rest, e.g. a gas boiler on a gas tariff while an EV charger or heat pump is priced on electricity, or a load with its own dynamic contract. Pass null/None for any load that should keep the shared tariff. Runtime parameter - not cached.

operating_hours_of_each_deferrable_load.Description: The total number of hours that each deferrable load should operate. Fractional values are accepted (e.g. 4.5) and scheduled as the exact nominal_power * hours of energy; for control finer than the optimization timestep use operating_timesteps_of_each_deferrable_load.

treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont.Description: When configuring a deferrable load, set treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont = True if the device should only switch fully on or off (for example, a basic hot water heater), or set treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont = False if the device supports variable power control within its range (for example, an EV charger with adjustable charging rate).

set_deferrable_load_single_constant.friendly_name: Deferrable load run single constant per optimization
set_deferrable_load_single_constant.Description: Define if we should set each deferrable load as a constant fixed value variable with just one startup for each optimization task

set_deferrable_startup_penalty.Description: For penalty P, each time the deferrable load turns on will incur an additional cost of nominal_power (kW) * cost_of_electricity * time step at that time

deferrable_load_max_cost.Description: Maximum acceptable cost for scheduling each deferrable load. If the cost to schedule the load (including startup penalty) exceeds this threshold, the load will not be scheduled. Set to 0 to disable and make load scheduling mandatory.

set_deferrable_max_startups.Description: Set the maximum number of times each deferrable load can be turned on during the optimization horizon. Set to 0 to disable this limit.

def_minimum_on_time.Description: Per-load minimum number of consecutive optimization timesteps a load must stay ON once started (min-up-time / short-cycle protection). One integer per deferrable load. Set to 0 (default) to disable for that load -- default-off, exact no-op. 1 timestep = optimization_time_step minutes (e.g. 3 timesteps at 30-min resolution = 90 minutes minimum run). Intended primarily for treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont loads (heat pumps, AC, pumps) where the ON/OFF binary is tightly coupled to the full nominal power. For plain/continuous-power loads the constraint holds the binary state ON but the power level may be fractional. Composes cleanly with set_deferrable_max_startups (independent constraints). Note: when the minimum ON window cannot fit within the load's operating-window end, the solver simply does not start the load for that horizon rather than forcing infeasibility.

def_minimum_off_time.Description: Per-load minimum number of consecutive optimization timesteps a load must stay OFF once it stops (min-down-time / short-cycle protection). One integer per deferrable load. Set to 0 (default) to disable for that load -- default-off, exact no-op. 1 timestep = optimization_time_step minutes (e.g. 3 timesteps at 30-min resolution = 90 minutes minimum off-time). Intended primarily for treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont loads (heat pumps, AC, compressors) where rapid ON-OFF-ON cycling causes wear or violates manufacturer limits. Composes cleanly with def_minimum_on_time and set_deferrable_max_startups (independent constraints). Note: when the minimum OFF window cannot fit within the remaining horizon, the solver simply defers the next start; the problem stays Optimal. Excludes single-constant and sequence loads (same gating as def_minimum_on_time).

publish_deferrable_load_states.Description: When true, EMHASS additionally publishes one interpretable command sensor per deferrable load (sensor.p_deferrableN_state) whose state is 'on', 'off' or 'variable' for the current timestep, with the full optimized on/off/variable plan as a 'schedule' attribute. This lets automations act on a clear command instead of thresholding the power forecast themselves. Defaults to false.

set_use_battery.Description: Set to True if we should consider an energy storage device such as a Li-Ion battery. Defaults to False

number_of_batteries.Description: Define the number of physical batteries in the plant. Defaults to 1. When greater than 1, every per-battery array parameter below (capacity, power limits, efficiencies, SOC min/max/target, stress cost, weight_battery_charge/discharge, SOC deficit/surplus threshold/cost) accepts either a single scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly this many entries. See docs/config.md for the full broadcast/nesting semantics.

battery_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases (System) is 2 or 3. Which physical phase(s) this battery's inverter is wired to - a fixed property of your installation. A single value (L1/L2/L3), or a '+'-joined combination (e.g. 'L1+L2', 'L1+L2+L3') for a genuinely multi-phase inverter - its power is then assumed evenly split across the named phases rather than counted on just one. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a single value (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries. Leave blank ('') to leave a battery out of the per-phase power cap entirely (the default).

sensor_power_battery.Description: The name of the signed AC-side battery power sensor in Watts from Home Assistant, used by battery self-identification. Either sign convention works (it is auto-detected). Only retrieved when set_use_battery_identification is true. For example: ‘sensor.power_battery’. With number_of_batteries > 1, provide a list of exactly number_of_batteries entity ids, one per battery, index-matched to the battery config lists; a single sensor is never broadcast to more than one battery.

sensor_battery_state_of_charge.Description: The name of the measured battery state of charge sensor in percent from Home Assistant, used by battery self-identification. Only retrieved when set_use_battery_identification is true. For example: ‘sensor.battery_state_of_charge’. With number_of_batteries > 1, provide a list of exactly number_of_batteries entity ids, one per battery, index-matched to the battery config lists; a single sensor is never broadcast to more than one battery.

set_use_battery_identification.Description: Opt-in, default off. When enabled, EMHASS learns the battery usable capacity and round-trip efficiency from Home Assistant history (signed battery power and measured state of charge) instead of relying only on the hand-entered values. It requires set_use_battery to be true and the sensor_power_battery and sensor_battery_state_of_charge sensors. In v1 this is advisory only: it never changes the configured battery values used by the optimizer. Defaults to false.

battery_identification_trust_tier.Description: Controls what battery self-identification does with its estimate. 'observe' (default) writes the estimate to a JSON file and the log only. 'suggest' additionally publishes two read-only Home Assistant sensors (identified capacity and round-trip efficiency) and logs a recommendation. Neither tier changes the configured battery values used by the optimizer. Defaults to 'observe'.

battery_identification_model_max_age.Description: Maximum age in hours before the battery identification estimate is re-fitted from fresh Home Assistant history. If the saved result is older than this value, a new estimate is produced. Set to 0 to force re-fitting on every call. Defaults to 24 hours (1 day).

set_nocharge_from_grid.Description: Set this to true if you want to forbid charging the battery from the grid. The battery will only be charged from excess PV

set_nodischarge_to_grid.friendly_name: Forbid battery discharge to the grid
set_nodischarge_to_grid.Description: Set this to true if you want to forbid discharging battery power to the grid.

set_battery_first_priority.Description: Set this to true to prefer draining stored battery energy before importing from the grid, so the battery is used up before any import while it is still above its minimum SoC. Useful on a flat (non time-of-use) tariff. This is a soft penalty, not a hard constraint: importing while the battery is charged is heavily penalized so drain-first wins on a flat tariff, but the optimizer can still import when that is the only feasible option, so it will not make the problem infeasible.

set_battery_dynamic.Description: Set a power dynamic limiting condition to the battery power. This is an additional constraint on the battery dynamic in power per unit of time (timestep), which allows you to set a percentage of the battery’s nominal full power as the maximum power allowed for (dis)charge.

battery_dynamic_max.friendly_name: Maximum percentage of battery discharge per hour
battery_dynamic_max.Description: The maximum positive (for discharge) allowed power variation (in percentage of battery maximum power) per hour. The solver will automatically scale this limit down based on your chosen timestep duration.

battery_dynamic_min.friendly_name: Maximum percentage of battery charge per hour
battery_dynamic_min.Description: The maximum negative (for charge) allowed power variation (in percentage of battery maximum power) per hour. The solver will automatically scale this limit down based on your chosen timestep duration.

weight_battery_discharge.friendly_name: Add cost weight for battery discharge
weight_battery_discharge.Description: An additional weight (currency/ kWh) applied in the cost function to battery usage for discharging. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast) or a list of one entry per battery, each entry itself a scalar or a time series - see docs/config.md for the nesting rules.

weight_battery_charge.friendly_name: Add cost weight for battery charge
weight_battery_charge.Description: An additional weight (currency/ kWh) applied in the cost function to battery usage for charging. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast) or a list of one entry per battery, each entry itself a scalar or a time series - see docs/config.md for the nesting rules.

battery_discharge_power_max.Description: The maximum discharge power in Watts. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_charge_power_max.Description: The maximum charge power in Watts. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_discharge_efficiency.Description: The discharge efficiency. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_charge_efficiency.Description: The charge efficiency. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_nominal_energy_capacity.Description: The total capacity of the battery stack in Wh. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_minimum_state_of_charge.Description: The minimum allowable battery state of charge. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_maximum_state_of_charge.Description: The maximum allowable battery state of charge. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_target_state_of_charge.Description: The desired battery state of charge at the end of each optimization cycle. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries; also the per-battery fallback target used by the soc_init/soc_final runtime chain.

battery_stress_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh) applied at the battery's nominal power to penalise high loads. Currently implemented as a quadratic curve (Cost ∝ Power²), incentivising 'low and slow' operation to reduce thermal stress and smooth power flows. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_stress_segments.Description: The number of linear segments used to approximate the stress cost curve. Higher values increase accuracy but may slightly increase computation time.

battery_soc_deficit_threshold.Description: The SOC threshold below which deficit penalties apply. For example, 0.20 for 20% SOC. Penalties are applied for every hour and every kWh the SOC is below this value. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_deficit_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh/h) applied for each kWh of SOC deficit per hour. This penalizes periods when the battery SOC falls below the deficit threshold. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_surplus_threshold.Description: The SOC threshold above which surplus penalties apply. For example, 0.90 for 90% SOC. Penalties are applied for every hour and every kWh the SOC is above this value. Use together with battery_soc_surplus_cost to discourage long dwell near full charge. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_surplus_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh/h) applied for each kWh of SOC above the surplus threshold per hour. This penalizes periods when the battery SOC sits above the surplus threshold, delaying charging into expected solar peaks and reducing time spent near full charge (battery longevity). Defaults to 0.0 (disabled). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

set_use_heatpump.Description: Set to true to enable heat pump optimization and thermal comfort scheduling.

heatpump_config_mode.Description: room_list: configure heating per room below (Rooms section), each using the model chosen in 'Thermal model family'. graph_topology: ignore the room list entirely and instead configure the whole heating system as a graph (Heat topology below) - lets you express hybrid setups (e.g. gas + heat pump feeding the same buffer) that a flat room list can't. Most single-heat-pump setups want room_list.

heatpump_multi_room_enabled.Description: Off (default): the Rooms tab shows one simplified room - just a target temperature and the essentials, nothing more to configure. On: the full Rooms tab, with per-room sensors, blind/door wiring, dispatch-model toggles and thermal coupling for as many independently-managed rooms as you need. Both write to the exact same underlying room configuration - this only changes how much of it the UI shows you.

heat_topology.Description: Only used when 'Configuration mode' above is graph_topology. Declarative directed graph of heat sources, thermal storage, consumers, and flows. When set, EMHASS compiles this into the flat optim_conf primitives (def_load_config, shared_thermal_tanks, deferrable_load_groups, cost_forecast_per_deferrable_load) automatically. Lets you express hybrid heating setups (gas + heat pump feeding the same DHW + buffer) without hand-rolling the deferrable-load indices. See docs/heat_topology.md for the schema.

is_electric_load.Description: Only used when 'Configuration mode' above is graph_topology. Per-deferrable-load boolean. True (default) means the load draws from the electric balance (heat pumps, electric heaters). False means the load consumes a non-electric commodity (gas, oil, district heating) and contributes only to its thermal target, not to the electric power balance. Auto-populated by the heat_topology compiler based on source type but can be overridden directly.

heatpump_model_family.Description: Per-room demand model used in room_list mode: simple (thermal-loss-only, the long-standing default), physics (real envelope/RC-network demand model using the per-room fields on the Rooms tab), machine_learning/deep_learning (selectable now, currently behave like simple - live dispatch integration for the two-stage/PINN models is a separate, future change).

heatpump_dl_model_name.Description: Placeholder for future deep-learning model selection.

heatpump_use_pinn.Description: Enable Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) based thermal forecasting.

heatpump_pinn_auto_train.Description: Automatically train the PINN model using historical data. No model path is required.

heatpump_pinn_lookahead.Description: Number of 15-minute steps forecast by the PINN model. Default is 144 (36 hours).

heatpump_ml_model_name.Description: Placeholder for future machine-learning model selection.

heatpump_ml_model_path.Description: Placeholder for future machine-learning model path.

heatpump_two_stage_data_csv.Description: CSV path used by the thermal two-stage planner (runtime history + weather/features). Relative paths are resolved from EMHASS root.

heatpump_two_stage_model_dir.Description: Directory containing classical thermal models and metadata for the two-stage planner.

heatpump_two_stage_horizon.Description: Planning horizon in timesteps used by coarse/fine two-stage evaluation.

heatpump_two_stage_top_k.Description: Number of best coarse models to pass to fine-stage selection.

heatpump_two_stage_coarse_models.Description: Optional model names (comma-separated per entry) to limit coarse-stage evaluation. Leave empty to auto-discover.

heatpump_two_stage_fine_models.Description: Optional model names (comma-separated per entry) to limit fine-stage evaluation. Leave empty to auto-discover.

heatpump_is_hybrid.Description: Enable if the system is hybrid (electric heat pump + gas boiler).

hybrid_heatpump_refit_enabled.friendly_name: Enable heat pump electric/gas model auto-refit
hybrid_heatpump_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit a physics-informed model of this heat pump's electric power draw (and gas consumption, if heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured) from weather/duty/history, against fresh Home Assistant history (hybrid-heatpump-model-refit action), and deploy it for hybrid-heatpump-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb, at least one Rooms-tab heatpump_room_temp_sensors entry (used as the fit target), and heatpump_power_sensor/heatpump_duty_sensor to be configured (used as fit inputs, not optional). Works for a pure-electric heat pump too - just leave heatpump_gas_meter_sensor empty and the gas part is skipped entirely. Informational only - this model is never read by the optimizer; if you want a thermal model that can actually change dispatch, see arx_model_refit_enabled and heatpump_room_self_learning_only (Rooms tab) instead.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each heat pump electric/gas model refit.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_max_electric_mae_w.Description: A refit is only deployed if its electric-power fit MAE (this field) - and, when a gas sensor is configured, its gas-consumption fit MAE too - is under the threshold(s), measured on a held-out slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_max_gas_mae_m3.Description: Only used when heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured (ignored for a pure-electric refit). A refit is only deployed if BOTH its gas-consumption fit MAE (this field) and its electric-power fit MAE are under their thresholds, measured on a held-out slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

hybrid_heatpump_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward electric-power forecast (and gas-consumption forecast, if the deployed model was fit with a gas sensor configured) using the fitted model (hybrid-heatpump-forecast action). Requires a deployed model (run hybrid-heatpump-model-refit at least once). Holds the last observed heat pump duty constant across the forecast horizon - a known simplification, not a claim of a planned dispatch schedule.

arx_model_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit an online-adaptive (RLS) multi-room model of electric power, gas consumption (if a gas sensor is configured), and every configured room's own temperature, against fresh Home Assistant history (arx-model-refit action), and deploy it for arx-model-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb, heatpump_power_sensor and heatpump_duty_sensor, plus at least one room with heatpump_room_temp_sensors configured. Rooms declared as coupled_neighbors of each other let the model learn a thermal coupling coefficient between them from history, in addition to the manually-entered heatpump_room_coupling_conductance - see arx_model_coupling_source for how the two relate. Unlike rc_model_refit_enabled/hybrid_heatpump_refit_enabled above (both informational only), a fit from this refit CAN change live dispatch for a given room - but only once that room's heatpump_room_self_learning_only (Rooms tab) is turned on; until then this model is informational too. Tuning (thermal-models-tune) searches this model's forgetting_factor/ridge and deploys immediately - it does not update these config defaults, so a later plain refit reverts to them unless you copy the winning values from the tune result into config yourself.

arx_model_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each ARX model refit.

arx_model_forgetting_factor.Description: Recursive-least-squares forgetting factor (0-1]. Lower values adapt faster to recent data but are noisier; 1.0 is a plain (non-forgetting) fit that weighs the whole refit window equally.

arx_model_ridge.Description: Initial RLS regularisation strength. Larger values start the fit more conservatively (slower initial adaptation, more resistant to noise); smaller values adapt faster but can overreact to a noisy start.

arx_model_refit_max_electric_mae_w.friendly_name: ARX model refit electric acceptance threshold
arx_model_refit_max_electric_mae_w.Description: A refit is only deployed if its electric-power fit MAE (this field), its gas-consumption fit MAE (when a gas sensor is configured), and every room's own temperature fit MAE are all under their thresholds, measured on a held-out chronological slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

arx_model_refit_max_gas_mae_m3.friendly_name: ARX model refit gas acceptance threshold
arx_model_refit_max_gas_mae_m3.Description: Only used when heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured (ignored for a pure-electric refit). Same held-out acceptance gate as the electric threshold above, for the gas-consumption fit.

arx_model_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward electric-power forecast (and gas-consumption forecast, if the deployed model has one) plus every configured room's own temperature forecast, using the fitted model (arx-model-forecast action). Requires a deployed model (run arx-model-refit at least once). Heat pump duty is resolved from the latest solved dispatch plan when one exists (a real, multi-room-aware trajectory), else the last observed heatpump_duty_sensor value held constant.

arx_model_coupling_enabled.Description: When on (default), rooms declared as heatpump_room_coupled_neighbors of each other get an extra feature in the ARX model fit so the model can learn a thermal coupling coefficient between them, in addition to their own temperature dynamics. When off, every room is fit independently (degrades gracefully to single-zone behaviour) - useful for a single-room install, or to rule out the coupling features while diagnosing a fit.

arx_model_coupling_source.Description: 'informational' (default): the learned per-pair coupling coefficient is only published/logged, so you can compare it against your own manually-entered heatpump_room_coupling_conductance - the manual value keeps driving real dispatch decisions unchanged. 'auto_dispatch': for any pair the learned model actually covers, its fitted coefficient overrides the manual value used by the live optimizer (heatpump_room_coupling_conductance stays as the fallback for any pair the learned model doesn't cover). Only switch to auto_dispatch once you've compared the two and trust the learned value - a room pair held at a near-constant temperature difference can produce an unreliable learned coefficient regardless of how much history is used.

arx_model_dispatch_max_cache_age_solves.Description: Only relevant when at least one room has 'Self-learning only' enabled and a fitted model. Driving dispatch directly from the fitted model requires a two-pass solve (a reference pass, then the real solve) because two of its fitted terms are non-linear products of duty and temperature that must first be evaluated against a known temperature trajectory. Re-using the previous solve's own trajectory as that reference (instead of re-running the reference pass every time) is safe for this many consecutive solves, since each room's starting temperature is re-pinned to its real sensor reading every solve regardless. Set to 0 or 1 to always run a fresh reference pass (slower, never stale).

arx_model_opening_relabel_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). At each arx-model-refit, for every room with NEITHER a heatpump_room_window_sensors NOR a heatpump_room_door_sensors entry configured, retroactively infer 'probably open' periods purely from that room's own thermal history (an offline forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass over one-step prediction residuals, repeated arx_model_opening_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into that room's own opening_x_outdoor feature. A room with either sensor configured is never touched by this, for any timestamp, at any iteration - it always uses its real sensor reading instead. This does not force every eligible room onto the relabeled data unconditionally: each refit also fits a same-refit baseline (no relabeling) and compares both on validation data, per room, deploying the relabel-enhanced version for a room only when it actually scores better there - see the refit result's rooms_using_relabel_enhancement.

arx_model_opening_relabel_iterations.Description: Only used when arx_model_opening_relabel_enabled is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop - higher values cost roughly one extra full model fit each, for diminishing returns.

arx_model_blind_relabel_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). At each arx-model-refit, for every room with NO heatpump_room_blind_sensors entry configured, retroactively infer a continuous (0=open..1=fully closed) blind/shading-position curve purely from that room's own thermal history on sunny periods (an offline forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass over one-step prediction residuals, repeated arx_model_blind_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into that room's own blind_x_dni feature. A room with a configured sensor is never touched by this, for any timestamp, at any iteration - it always uses its real sensor reading instead. Blind position is only ever observable when there is sun (dni) to block or not - a room with too little sunny history in the refit window (e.g. heatpump_weather_dni_sensor left unconfigured) is skipped for that refit rather than guessed at. This does not force every eligible room onto the relabeled data unconditionally: each refit also fits a same-refit baseline (no relabeling) and compares both on validation data, per room, deploying the relabel-enhanced version for a room only when it actually scores better there - see the refit result's rooms_using_relabel_enhancement.

arx_model_blind_relabel_iterations.Description: Only used when arx_model_blind_relabel_enabled is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop. One higher than the opening-relabel default by design: the first pass here is a weaker heuristic bootstrap (no fitted blind_x_dni coefficient exists yet), so one extra calibrated pass meaningfully improves on that weaker start.

arx_model_blind_estimate_source.friendly_name: Live blind-position estimate: informational vs. dispatch
arx_model_blind_estimate_source.Description: 'informational' (default): the live Kalman-inferred blind-position estimate (see arx_model_blind_relabel_enabled and the 'Blind Position Estimate' sensor per room) is only computed/persisted/published every naive-mpc-optim cycle, so you can compare it against your own knowledge of when blinds were actually closed - it never reaches the optimizer, which keeps using its existing static blind_position fallback for that room. 'auto_dispatch': for a room whose estimate currently clears its own confidence gate (needs several consecutive sunny cycles of consistent evidence after a good arx_model_blind_relabel_enabled refit - a fresh/uncertain estimate is never used), the live estimate overrides the static fallback for that solve. A wrong blind-position guess has no safe direction (unlike pausing heat for a possibly-open window) - only switch to auto_dispatch once you've compared informational readings against reality and trust them. A room's real heatpump_room_blind_sensors reading, when configured, always takes precedence over any estimate regardless of this setting.

arx_model_opening_confirm_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). Requires arx_model_opening_relabel_enabled to actually be useful. For each room with neither a window nor a door sensor configured, once its EM relabeling has surfaced a candidate opening event, publish a question sensor (sensor.room_opening_confirmation_<room>) asking whether that event really was an open window/door - pair a Home Assistant automation (see docs/automations.md) with 'Room opening confirmation: ready/answer input_boolean' (above) to let you answer from a notification. A confirmed answer becomes permanent ground truth: it's never re-inferred or overwritten by any later refit.

heatpump_can_cool.Description: Enable if the heat pump supports both heating and cooling.

heatpump_dispatch_control_entity.friendly_name: Whole-house heat pump on/off entity (HA entity)
heatpump_dispatch_control_entity.Description: Home Assistant switch entity_id for the whole-house heat pump's on/off control. EMHASS never calls this entity's service directly - it only publishes a dispatch target sensor for a companion HA automation to apply. Its live init-temperature and the rc-model-refit/hybrid-heatpump-model-refit physics fits all reuse the first configured Rooms-tab heatpump_room_temp_sensors entry - at least one room with a sensor must be configured for any of these whole-house features to work.

heatpump_dispatch_min_temperature.Description: Minimum indoor temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_max_temperature.Description: Maximum indoor temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_target_temperature.Description: Fallback target indoor temperature for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_nominal_power.Description: Nominal heating power of the whole-house heat pump, used by the thermal_battery model for the dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_supply_temperature.Description: Heating supply/flow temperature used to estimate the heat pump COP for the dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_volume.Description: Effective volume used by the thermal_battery model to convert heat input into a temperature change for the dispatch load.

heatpump_weather_use_own_sensors.Description: On (default): each weather field below (outdoor temperature, wind, GHI/DNI/DHI) uses its own configured sensor where one is set, and falls back to Open-Meteo's historical weather data for any field left blank - no behavior change if every field is already filled in. Off: Open-Meteo is used for all of them regardless of what's configured, useful when a specific sensor (e.g. an outdoor temperature probe in direct sun) is unreliable rather than simply missing.

heatpump_weather_ghi_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for global horizontal irradiance (GHI).

heatpump_weather_dni_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for direct normal irradiance (DNI).

heatpump_weather_dhi_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI).

heatpump_weather_wind_speed_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for wind speed.

heatpump_weather_wind_direction_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for wind direction.

heatpump_weather_humidity_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for relative humidity.

heatpump_power_sensor.friendly_name: Heat pump electric power sensor (HA entity)
heatpump_power_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for real-time heat pump electrical power in watts. A cumulative kWh energy meter also works - refits automatically detect a cumulative reading (values that only ever rise) and convert it to an average power in W (assuming the meter's cumulative unit is kWh) before fitting. Also used live during naive-mpc-optim (together with the duty sensor below) by the sensorless window/door-open Kalman detector, to know how much heat was actually delivered since the last dispatch cycle.

heatpump_flow_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for measured heating circuit flow temperature in °C.

heatpump_blind_position_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the whole-house blind/shading position (0=open..1=closed), used only by the thermal-mass physics model (rc-model-refit/rc-model-forecast) to gate the window-transmitted solar-gain pathway - the opaque-exterior-wall solar pathway is never gated by this, since interior blinds can't affect what hits the outside of the building. Held flat at the last live reading for the rc-model-forecast horizon. Leave empty to treat blinds as always fully open (pre-existing behavior) - see 'Enable retroactive blind-position relabeling' below for a sensorless alternative when you don't have this sensor.

heatpump_door_window_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the whole-house door/window open state (0=closed..1=open), used only by the thermal-mass physics model (rc-model-refit) as an extra ventilation-loss gate on top of the existing wind-driven envelope loss. Leave empty to treat doors/windows as always closed (pre-existing behavior) - see 'Enable retroactive door/window-opening relabeling' below for a sensorless alternative when you don't have this sensor.

heatpump_facade_azimuth_deg.Description: Compass direction the house's main heat-gaining window/facade faces, in degrees (0=north, 90=east, 180=south, 270=west), used by the thermal-mass physics model to project solar irradiance onto that facade. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data. Filling in a known/estimated value does NOT lock it - it becomes a strong starting point/anchor that the fit is regularised toward (much harder to drift away from than an unconfigured value), but real, sustained data can still move it if your estimate turns out to be off.

heatpump_facade_tilt_deg.Description: Tilt of the house's main heat-gaining window/facade from horizontal, in degrees (0=flat/skylight, 90=vertical wall/window), used by the thermal-mass physics model to project solar irradiance onto that facade. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data. Filling in a known/estimated value does NOT lock it - same strong-anchor-not-hard-lock behavior as 'Main window/facade azimuth' above.

heatpump_facade2_azimuth_deg.Description: Compass direction of a SECOND heat-gaining window/facade that faces a different way than the main one above (e.g. a dakraam/skylight or a window in a different room covered by the same indoor temperature sensor), in degrees (0=north, 90=east, 180=south, 270=west). Only used when 'Second facade weight' below is nonzero. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data - filling in a known/estimated value makes it a strong starting anchor rather than a hard lock (same behavior as 'Main window/facade azimuth').

heatpump_facade2_tilt_deg.Description: Tilt of the second window/facade from horizontal, in degrees (0=flat/skylight, 90=vertical wall/window). Only used when 'Second facade weight' below is nonzero. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data - filling in a known/estimated value makes it a strong starting anchor rather than a hard lock.

heatpump_facade2_weight.Description: How much the second window/facade above contributes to solar gain, relative to the main facade (e.g. 0.5 if it's roughly half the window area of the main facade). This is always a value YOU set, never fitted - the model can't tell relative window area apart from a temperature signal alone. Leave empty/0 to disable this second facade entirely (the default - single-facade behavior, unchanged).

heatpump_facade3_azimuth_deg.Description: Compass direction of a THIRD heat-gaining window/facade, same role as the second facade's azimuth above (e.g. a window facing yet another direction, covered by the same indoor temperature sensor). Only used when 'Third facade weight' below is nonzero. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data - filling in a known/estimated value makes it a strong starting anchor rather than a hard lock.

heatpump_facade3_tilt_deg.Description: Tilt of the third window/facade from horizontal, in degrees (0=flat/skylight, 90=vertical wall/window). Only used when 'Third facade weight' below is nonzero. Leave empty to let rc-model-refit fit this freely from data - filling in a known/estimated value makes it a strong starting anchor rather than a hard lock.

heatpump_facade3_weight.Description: How much the third window/facade above contributes to solar gain, relative to the main facade - same role as 'Second facade weight' above, always a value YOU set, never fitted. Leave empty/0 to disable this third facade entirely (the default).

heatpump_building_mass_class.Description: How heavy/massive the building's construction is (very_light e.g. lightweight timber frame, light, medium, heavy, very_heavy e.g. solid masonry/concrete) - used as a starting-point anchor for the thermal-mass physics model's own mass_tau_h (interior thermal mass time constant), based on ISO 13790's own building heat-capacity classification. Like facade orientation, this is a strong anchor, NOT a hard lock - rc-model-refit can still learn a different value if real data clearly disagrees. Floor area is deliberately not asked for here - it cancels out of the calculation and would not change the result. Leave empty to fit mass_tau_h freely from data, same as today.

heatpump_emitter_type.Description: The type of heat emitter (convector, radiator, floor_heating) - used as a starting-point anchor for the thermal-mass physics model's own tau_emit_h (heat-emitter response time), a strong anchor rather than a hard lock, same as facade orientation and building thermal mass above. Only fill this in if EVERY room covered by the indoor temperature sensor uses the SAME emitter type - if you have a mix (e.g. some rooms on floor heating, others on radiators), leave this empty and let the model fit one blended value from data instead of guessing which type dominates.

heatpump_gas_meter_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for gas usage when hybrid operation is enabled. Either a raw cumulative meter totalizer (the usual state_class=total_increasing HA convention) or an already-incremental consumption-per-interval sensor works - refits automatically detect a cumulative reading (values that only ever rise) and convert it to a per-interval delta before fitting.

heatpump_outdoor_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for measured outdoor temperature history, used to fit/refit the thermal-mass physics model (rc-model-refit action).

heatpump_duty_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the heat pump's measured on/off or duty-cycle state history, used to fit/refit the thermal-mass physics model (rc-model-refit action). Also used live during naive-mpc-optim by the sensorless window/door-open Kalman detector - see 'Heat pump electric power sensor' above.

heatpump_target_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the target thermostat temperature. Visible only when control strategy is 'thermostat_sensor'.

heatpump_max_deviation.Description: Maximum allowed deviation from the weather curve flow temperature.

rc_model_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward indoor-temperature forecast (heating assumed off) and a 'heating needed by' sensor, using the fitted thermal-mass physics model. Requires data/rc_model_params.json to exist (fit it once with scripts/thermal_mass_physics_model.py).

rc_model_forecast_horizon_hours.Description: How far forward to simulate the indoor temperature. Requesting a horizon longer than the weather forecast actually returned (controlled by delta_forecast_daily on the triggering call) is logged as a mismatch rather than failing.

rc_model_forecast_comfort_min_temp.Description: Indoor temperature below which 'heating needed by' fires. Compared against the forecast after the safety margin below is subtracted.

rc_model_forecast_safety_margin_c.Description: Defensive offset subtracted from the simulated temperature before the comfort-floor check, so the warning fires earlier rather than later. The physics model has a confirmed tendency to run warm in open-loop simulation.

rc_model_forecast_model_selection.Description: Only relevant when BOTH 'Enable RC model forecast' and 'Enable ARX model forecast' are on - both predict room temperature, so only ONE actually needs to run and publish its sensors. 'auto' compares each model's own last-deployed held-out accuracy (RC's whole-house val_mae_c vs. the ARX model's mean per-room room_temp_mae_c - no re-fitting needed) and uses whichever is more accurate; a family that has never successfully deployed loses by default. Pin to 'rc_model' or 'arx_model' to always use that one regardless of accuracy. When only one of the two forecasts is enabled, this setting has no effect - that one just runs.

rc_model_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit the thermal-mass physics model's parameters against fresh Home Assistant history (rc-model-refit action) and deploy them for rc-model-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb (see docs/passing_data.md) since the refit window is longer than Home Assistant's own recorder retention. Informational only - this model is never read by the optimizer; if you want a thermal model that can actually change dispatch, see arx_model_refit_enabled and heatpump_room_self_learning_only (Rooms tab) instead.

rc_model_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each refit.

rc_model_refit_max_mae_c.Description: A refit is only deployed (overwrites the previous fitted parameters) if its room-temperature fit MAE is under this value. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous parameters are left in place, protecting against deploying a fit from e.g. a sensor outage during the refit window.

rc_model_refit_door_relabel_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). Only relevant when 'Door/window open sensor' (above) is NOT configured. At each rc-model-refit, retroactively infer 'probably open' periods purely from the model's own thermal residuals (a teacher-forced one-step forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass, repeated rc_model_refit_door_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into the model's door-open ventilation-loss term. This never overrides a configured sensor's own reading. Each refit also fits a same-refit baseline (no relabeling) and compares both on held-out validation data, deploying the relabel-enhanced version only when it actually scores better there - see the refit result's relabel_source.

rc_model_refit_door_relabel_iterations.Description: Only used when 'Enable retroactive door/window-opening relabeling' is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop - higher values cost roughly one extra full model fit each, for diminishing returns.

rc_model_refit_blind_relabel_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). Only relevant when 'Blind/shading position sensor' (above) is NOT configured. At each rc-model-refit, retroactively infer a continuous (0=open..1=fully closed) blind/shading-position curve purely from the model's own thermal residuals on sunny periods (a teacher-forced one-step forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass, repeated rc_model_refit_blind_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into the model's window-solar-gain term. This never overrides a configured sensor's own reading, and is skipped for a refit window with too little sunny history to say anything. Each refit also fits a same-refit baseline (no relabeling) and compares both on held-out validation data, deploying the relabel-enhanced version only when it actually scores better there - see the refit result's relabel_source.

rc_model_refit_blind_relabel_iterations.Description: Only used when 'Enable retroactive blind-position relabeling' is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop.

rc_model_refit_phase_robust_enabled.Description: Opt-in (default off). The thermal-mass physics model fits in ~24h segments, each reset from real data at its own start - by default always at the SAME time-of-day boundary for every refit (a 'multiple shooting' segmentation, in the ODE-parameter-estimation sense), which can quietly bias the result toward whatever time-of-day happens to land on segment boundaries - the same reasoning behind varying fold start-times in walk-forward time-series validation. When on, every fit in the refit chain (the final baseline/door/blind/both scoring fits, and the internal fits used to infer door/blind-position labels) instead becomes a single JOINT fit whose residuals span 'Number of fit phases' different segment-start offsets at once, so one shared parameter set has to explain the data under every phase alignment simultaneously. Cheaper than fitting each phase separately and picking the best: still only 3 restarts per fit, each just costing roughly 'Number of fit phases' times more to evaluate - off by default since it still adds real compute to a routinely-scheduled action.

rc_model_refit_num_phases.Description: Only used when 'Enable phase-robust fitting' is on. How many evenly-spaced segment-start offsets each joint fit's residual vector spans.

rc_model_refit_fit_electric_power_enable.Description: Opt-in (default off). Only takes effect when 'Heat pump power sensor' is configured. When on, every fit in the refit/tune chain ALSO has to explain the room's real electric-power draw, not just its temperature - a Carnot-lift COP model (same formula as the existing heat-pump dispatch models) converts the thermal output the model already tracks into predicted Watts, and two new parameters (a COP efficiency factor and a Watts-per-unit scale) are fit against the real sensor alongside the usual 25. Publishes an extra 'Heating Electric Power Forecast' sensor once enabled. Off by default since it changes what the fit optimizes for - only turn on once you're happy with the temperature-only fit quality.

heatpump_number_of_units.Description: How many separate physical heat pump units this house has. Almost always 1 - only increase this if you genuinely have more than one independent heat pump (e.g. one per wing of the house), each with its own nominal power and control strategy.

heatpump_unit_name.Description: A short, recognizable name for this heat pump unit.

heatpump_unit_nominal_power.Description: Maximum electrical input power of this heat pump unit in watts. Used for the shared-power-group cap for rooms assigned to this unit (see 'Room heat pump unit' in Rooms), and as this unit's own contribution to the whole-house aggregate duty signal.

heatpump_unit_control_mode.Description: fixed (default): rooms on this unit use their own static 'Room supply temperature'. weather_curve: only for a room with 'Self-learning only' also on - lets the optimizer treat that room's supply/flow temperature as a genuine decision variable, bounded by this unit's own weather curve below, instead of a frozen constant. Requires the room to be the only heatpump_group_member sharing this unit; a room sharing this unit with others falls back to fixed behavior with a visible note in its own refit/tune/forecast results.

heatpump_unit_curve_slope.Description: Only used when this unit's 'Control strategy' is weather_curve. Weather-curve slope: supply_temp = slope × outdoor_temp + intercept. Typically negative (e.g. -1.0): colder outdoor temperature leads to higher supply temperature.

heatpump_unit_curve_intercept.Description: Only used when this unit's 'Control strategy' is weather_curve. Weather-curve intercept: supply_temp = slope × outdoor_temp + intercept.

heatpump_unit_supply_temp_min.Description: Only used when this unit's 'Control strategy' is weather_curve. Lower bound the optimizer may pick for this unit's supply temperature, regardless of what the weather curve alone would give.

heatpump_unit_supply_temp_max.Description: Only used when this unit's 'Control strategy' is weather_curve. Upper bound the optimizer may pick for this unit's supply temperature, regardless of what the weather curve alone would give.

heatpump_number_of_rooms.Description: Number of controlled rooms. This defines how many room tabs and room-level sensor entries are used.

heatpump_room_names.Description: List of room names used for room sub-tab labels. Keep the same order as room sensor arrays.

heatpump_room_phase.Description: Only used when number_of_phases (System) is 2 or 3. Which physical phase(s) this room's electrical heating draw is wired to - a fixed property of your home's wiring. A single value (L1/L2/L3), or a '+'-joined combination (e.g. 'L1+L2' for a 2-phase compressor, 'L1+L2+L3' for a fully 3-phase one) for a heat pump wired across more than one phase - its power is then assumed evenly split across the named phases rather than counted on just one. Leave blank ('') to leave this room out of the per-phase power cap entirely (the default).
